result.summary: The image depicts a large, multi-lane commercial intersection with significant crossing distances and high traffic exposure. While basic infrastructure like marked crosswalks and curb ramps are present, the environment lacks pedestrian refuge islands and visible dedicated pedestrian signals, prioritizing vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to multiple lanes of traffic for an extended period without a safe place to stop.

hazards.name: Multi-lane Threat
hazards.description: Multiple lanes of traffic in the same direction increase the risk of a pedestrian being struck by a vehicle in an adjacent lane that is obscured by a stopped vehicle.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes approaching the intersection

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages, reducing exposure time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks, but lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and refuge islands. The wide roadway and commercial setting suggest a high-volume traffic environment with significant exposure for pedestrians during crossings.

hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No visible pedestrian-specific signals to indicate when it is safe to cross, forcing reliance on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals and improve predictability.

result.summary: The environment is a wide commercial corridor with basic pedestrian infrastructure including a marked crosswalk and curb ramps. However, the large crossing distance, lack of visible pedestrian signals, and expansive parking lot entrances create significant conflict points and exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: The large, undefined entrance to the commercial parking lot creates multiple points of potential conflict between turning vehicles and pedestrians on the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add street trees or a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway/parking lot to improve comfort and safety.
